content_text:
I wanted to turn this tablet into a real second monitor, so I built it.

Here is the desk setup: laptop on the left, primary external display behind it, and an Android tablet running Windows extended desktop natively at 2560x1600 over a single USB cable.

The catch: the tablet's fixed-function video decoder flatly refused a single 2560x1600 frame (capped at 14,400 macroblocks vs 16,000 needed). But the GPU had no trouble driving the panel.

So the pipeline splits each frame into two horizontal 2560x800 strips, encodes them concurrently with NVENC, and streams them across an adb tunnel to two MediaCodec instances decoding side-by-side.

Among the configurations tested, splitting the frame into two encoded regions produced the best full-frame result — holding 45.3 fps sustained over USB with zero dropped frames, 20.0 Mbit/s average bitrate, and 48 ms median latency.
